About Taarak Mehta Ka Ooltah Chashmah: 
----------------------------------------------------------------------
The show is inspired by the famous humorous column 'Duniya Ne Undha Chasma' by the eminent Gujarati writer Mr. Tarak Mehta. This story evolves around happenings in "Gokuldham Co-operative Society" and covers topical issues that are socially relevant. The show predominantly - revolves around 'Jethalal' (Dilip Joshi), an uneducated Gujarati businessman. Your 'Taarak Mehta' (Sailesh Lodha), is his neighbour. 'Jethalal' finds a friend and philosopher in 'Taarak Mehta' and often goes to him for advice whenever he is in trouble. Jethalal's family includes his simpleton wife 'Daya Ben' (Disha Wakani) and a mischievous son 'Tapu' (Bhavya Gandhi). Tapu is a menace and a constant source of trouble for all the members of Gokuldham. They have often warned 'Jethalal' to reform 'Tapu' or be prepared to leave the premises. Lost hopes of being heard by his son, he calls his father 'Champaklal' (Amit Bhatt) from the village. This was his great idea of leashing some control over the mischievous Tapu. The opposite happens and the grandfather joins hands with the grandson to make life a roller coaster troublesome ride for Jethalal.

She beats before she talks but now she has to solve all cases through reconciliation. Santosh Sharma is a young new recruit and a typical lonely girl in the city. The head of the pack is S.H.O Haseena Mallik, witty, romantic leads by example. The common challenge for all these women is to bring sensitivity to their policing while dealing with cases that come to this police station. Hence their solution is most unusual. snippet.title: Govardhan, Mathura Food Tour I ब्रजभूमि का असली स्वाद I Aloo Kachori, Rabri, Khurchan, Sev Paratha
snippet.description:
Holi in Govardhan is a time of colors, devotion, and delicious food. The streets are filled with the aroma of freshly fried snacks and traditional sweets. We set out on a street food tour to experience the best local flavors before the festival.  

Our first stop was Harilal Kachori Wale. We had aalu kachori with chutney, a quick and satisfying breakfast. The kachoris were freshly fried in mustard oil, making them crisp and flavorful.  

Next, we visited Shree Nath Ji Misthan Bhandar. If you love rabri, this place is a must-visit. Fresh batches were being made at regular intervals. We were lucky to taste some straight from the kadai. It was thick, creamy, and delicious.  

Chirag Namkeen Bhandar was our next stop. We tried some of their best-selling namkeen, including mota mixture, hing mixture, dal biji, sev, and saloni. Each had a unique taste and crunch.  

At Shree Giriraj Misthan Bhandar, we had bedai kachori with sabzi and chutney. The kachoris were stuffed with moong dal and fried in ghee. The pumpkin sabzi was much loved for its mild sweetness, making the meal even more special. Everything here, from the bedai to the sweets, was prepared in ghee, adding to the rich flavors.  

Shree Govardhan Misthan Bhandar had a variety of sweet and savory snacks. Their aalu tikki chaat was the highlight. The tikki was super crisp, topped with matra, dahi, and chutneys. Every bite was packed with flavor.  

We stopped at Gopal Ji Kanji Vada Stall for a bowl of refreshing kanji vada. The vadas were soaked in tangy mustard-flavored kanji, making it a light yet flavorful dish.  

In the evening, we returned to Shree Giriraj Misthan Bhandar for their samosas. These were one of Anubhav’s favorites. The crisp casing and zesty fried potato filling made them a perfect evening snack.  

Chauni Chacha Parathe Wale was next. Parathas are a filling option, and we tried their sev paratha. Sev, a crunchy namkeen, was mixed with a potato filling and stuffed into the paratha. It was unique and delicious.  

At Shree Giriraj Jalpan Grih, we stopped for a cup of chai. This place is one of our favorites for tea. They also serve coffee and lassi, making it a great spot to relax.  

We wrapped up our food tour at Lala Paan Bhandar. A flavorful paan was the perfect way to end our journey through the festive streets of Govardhan.

snippet.title: MASSIVE Lucknowi Muslim WEDDING Dawat FOOD I Fish & Raan Musallam + Lagan Ka Murgh + Mutton Pulao
snippet.description:
Weddings in Lucknow are not just about uniting two people but about celebrating tradition, culture, and of course, food. This time, we had the privilege of attending the Dawate Walima celebrations of two newlywed couples—Yasub & Sakina and Nida & Amber. These grand feasts, deeply rooted in Awadhi heritage, bring families and friends together over an elaborate spread of meticulously prepared dishes.

What made these feasts even more special was that the head chefs at both weddings were two brothers—Mohd. Arik and Arshi—culinary maestros who belong to a family that has been perfecting the art of Awadhi wedding feasts for six generations. Their reputation precedes them, with families who take pride in hosting grand meals placing their trust in their expertise. Through their craft, they have kept alive the rich culinary heritage of the region.

We visited both venues to witness the massive preparations taking place behind the scenes. Lucknowites are known for their deep appreciation of good food, so everything had to be executed with precision. Arik and Arshi took charge of the entire process, supervising every step, from marination to the final presentation. As they worked, they explained the intricate details of an Awadhi dawat, and we followed them through the making of some of the most iconic dishes—shahi tukda, sheermal, raan musallam, fish musallam, galouti kebab, and mutton pulao. Watching these dishes come to life firsthand was a true revelation of the expertise, passion and relentless hard work that goes into creating an unforgettable feast.

As evening set in, guests started arriving, and we began our culinary journey at Yasub and Sakina’s wedding venue. There, we had the privilege of tasting raan musallam, fish musallam, and galouti kebab right at the cooking area, in the company of the chefs. Later, we joined the guests to enjoy a delicious spread of rich qorma paired with soft, fragrant naan. Every dish was a testament to slow cooking, perfected over time, and brimming with complex flavors.

Next, we made our way to Nida and Amber’s wedding feast. The spread was equally magnificent, starting with galouti kebabs, chicken tikka, and chicken reshmi kebabs. For the main course, we indulged in rogan josh, lagan ka murgh, and the ever-fragrant mutton pulao. The feast ended on a sweet note with decadent shahi tukda and refreshing kulfi—each bite a delightful blend of tradition and indulgence.

Beyond the remarkable food, what stood out was the warmth and generosity of the hosts. And as we relished each dish, we realized that in Lucknow, feeding people is not just a custom—it’s a cherished tradition, upheld with pride and passion.


Mezbaan Catering Services, Lucknow.

snippet.title: Ultimate Puri Food Tour | Dalma, Dahi Bara Aloo Dum, Khaja & More | Veggie Paaji
snippet.description:
Veggie Paaji is taking you on the ultimate food tour of Puri - The Land of Jagannath 🙏 Get ready for a non-stop flavour festival as we uncover the absolute best vegetarian street food and traditional sweets this sacred city has to offer. We're on a mission to find the "Asli Swaad" (The Real Taste), and trust us, we found it!

Join our ultimate food challenge as we dive into:

➡️ Dahi Bara Aloo Dum: Our first stop in Puri was for this legendary street food! We found an amazing vendor serving incredibly soft lentil fritters (bara) topped with spicy potato curry (aloo dum) and a flavourful pea curry (ghugni). One bite and we were in heaven! 🤤

➡️ Authentic Odia Thali: This is the definition of a true vegetarian feast! With over 10 items like Dalma, Saaga Bhaja, Aloo Chokha, and a rich Mushroom Curry, this thali offers an authentic taste of Odisha in every single bite. So filling, yet our hearts wanted more! 😍

➡️ Spicy Beachside Jhal Muri: You can't visit Golden Beach without trying this! A fiery, tangy, and crunchy puffed rice snack that is an absolute explosion of flavour. Seriously amazing! 🔥

➡️ Famous Khaja Prasad: Near the Jagannath temple, we tried the famous sweet prasad, Khaja. This crispy, flaky pastry soaked in sugar syrup is divinely delicious and simply melts in your mouth.

➡️ Puri's Unique Papodi: This is a dessert you've never seen before! Made from delicate layers of milk cream (malai) and thickened sweet milk (rabri), this sweet left us speechless. We have to come back just for this!

That was our non-stop food tour of Puri! What was your favourite dish? Let us know in the comments below!

snippet.title: 24 Hours Eating Old Delhi’s BEST Street Food | Delhi Food Walks
snippet.description:
►SUBSCRIBE for 2 new videos every week: https://
www.youtube.com/user/TheMrtaster
►Uzbekistan Food Tour- Iconic Upside Down Uzbeki Bread in Samarkand: https://youtu.be/JJNu_3X3L3A

Join me and my good friend Delhi Food Walks as we explore the vibrant streets of Old Delhi, tasting some of the most iconic and flavorful street foods India has to offer! From sizzling kebabs to royal desserts, this tour is packed with culture, tradition, and unforgettable flavors.

🫓 What I Tried:
 • Khasta Kachori & Aloo Sabzi – Crispy lentil-filled snack with spicy potato curry, masala, and green chili.
 • Golden Indian Tea – Made with milk, tea, sugar, spices, almonds, and saffron.
 • 150-Year-Old Paratha Shop – Parathas with chutneys like pumpkin, aloo mutter, sweet mango powder sauce, and Rabri-filled sweet paratha.
 • Bedmi Poori, Chole Bhature & Samosa with Jalebi – Puffy breads with chickpeas, chutneys, and desserts like Halwa, Jalebi, and Gulab Jamun.
 • Rabri Falooda – A chilled dessert with milk, cardamom, sugar, nuts, and ice.
 • Paan – Traditional betel leaf mouth freshener with colorful fillings.
 • Qureshi Kababs at Jama Masjid – Juicy grilled koobideh, chicken, and beef kebabs, sizzling on charcoal, topped with butter.
 • Chicken Lollipop at Rafiq Chicken Corner – Spicy fried chicken with unmatched flavor.
 • Haji Mohd Hussain’s Fried Chicken – Street-style fried chicken with onion, lemon, and masala.
 • Buffalo Biryani at Mohd Taufiq – Rich and flavorful biryani served hot in Jama Masjid.
 • Shahi Tukda at Cool Point – Traditional dessert with ghee-soaked bread, mango & vanilla ice cream, saffron, almonds, and silver foil.

🎥 This food journey was one of my favorite experiences in India – full of colors, spices, and warmth. Don’t miss this one!

Join me and my good friend Delhi Food Walks as we explore the vibrant streets of Old Delhi, tasting some of the most iconic and flavorful street foods India has to offer! From sizzling kebabs to royal desserts, this tour is packed with culture, tradition, and unforgettable flavors.

🫓 What I Tried:
 • Khasta Kachori & Aloo Sabzi – Crispy lentil-filled snack with spicy potato curry, masala, and green chili.
 • Golden Indian Tea – Made with milk, tea, sugar, spices, almonds, and saffron.
 • 150-Year-Old Paratha Shop – Parathas with chutneys like pumpkin, aloo mutter, sweet mango powder sauce, and Rabri-filled sweet paratha.
 • Bedmi Poori, Chole Bhature & Samosa with Jalebi – Puffy breads with chickpeas, chutneys, and desserts like Halwa, Jalebi, and Gulab Jamun.
 • Rabri Falooda – A chilled dessert with milk, cardamom, sugar, nuts, and ice.
 • Paan – Traditional betel leaf mouth freshener with colorful fillings.
 • Qureshi Kababs at Jama Masjid – Juicy grilled koobideh, chicken, and beef kebabs, sizzling on charcoal, topped with butter.
 • Chicken Lollipop at Rafiq Chicken Corner – Spicy fried chicken with unmatched flavor.
 • Haji Mohd Hussain’s Fried Chicken – Street-style fried chicken with onion, lemon, and masala.
 • Buffalo Biryani at Mohd Taufiq – Rich and flavorful biryani served hot in Jama Masjid.
 • Shahi Tukda at Cool Point – Traditional dessert with ghee-soaked bread, mango & vanilla ice cream, saffron, almonds, and silver foil.

🎥 This food journey was one of my favorite experiences in India – full of colors, spices, and warmth. Don’t miss this one!

snippet.description:
This is day 1 of me trying out the various categories of different food items available in the market, ranging from the cheapest to the most expensive versions of those food items. In this video I’ll be trying out the various versions of one of the most popular street food in Delhi, Momos. Momos are arguably the most loved street food in Delhi and is can be found at the corner of almost every street in this city. Various categories of momos are available in Delhi, the most popular one being the cheapest variety which is readily available and is generally priced very reasonably. Other varieties of momos include but are not limited to tandoori momos, Kurkure momos and the expensive high quality steamed dimsums. Surprisingly, all these food items were extremely flavourful and unique in their own way. I had a great time trying out these food items. Hope you guys enjoy the video !
